Visited Oye Kake for my birthday dinner with my wife, choosing the place based on its strong Google reviews. We weren’t looking for anything too fancy, just a place to enjoy some good food. But the experience ended up being a bit disappointing.
The chur chur naan was not properly cooked, which was quite a letdown. The Jain kofta also didn’t meet expectations. While I understand Jain preparation has limitations, I don’t think that should compromise the taste to this extent.
On the positive side, the paneer starter (don’t recall the exact name) was excellent and definitely the highlight of our meal.
The ambience was great and added nicely to the overall experience, but unfortunately, the food didn’t quite match up.
Overall, an average experience: good vibe, but the food quality needs improvement.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Taste of Kerala in Fort and absolutely loved the experience. The restaurant serves authentic Kerala-style food and everything we ordered was delicious.

We tried Chicken Chettinad, Chicken 65, and another chicken starter (don’t remember the name), and all of them were extremely tasty. The Chicken 65 was quite different from the usual version we get it had a unique Kerala-style flavor which made it even better.

They also serve complimentary curries, pickle, mirchi, papad, and a salad made with onion, amla, and mango in a vinegar-style dressing. Even these sides were so flavorful and really added to the meal.

Overall, the food was amazing and satisfying. If you enjoy Kerala cuisine, this place is definitely a must-try.

featured_reviews.name: Ankita Choudhary
featured_reviews.review_text: Decent family apt ambience, good selection of Kerala menu, authentic taste and reasonably priced items. Family as well as friends can visit. We ordered Kadala curry (black gram curry), veg stew, idiyappam, Kerala wheat parotta, and veg korma. We also got complimentary payasam for dessert. Over all, good experience. I would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Saurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered veg biryani from Taste of Kerala on 13 October 2025, but I was delivered chicken biryani instead. This is a serious issue, especially for someone who does not eat non-veg.
I immediately went to the restaurant and showed them the delivered order. They said the owner was not present and asked me to return the food and come back the next day for a refund. I trusted them and handed over the food.
When I returned the next day, the owner refused to take responsibility and told me to contact Zomato instead. This was extremely unprofessional and dishonest.
This is not just a mistake—it’s a serious concern when non-veg food is served while claiming it is veg. Please be very careful. If the intention was to avoid a refund, they could have been honest instead of wasting my time.
I do not recommend this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Rituka Nakhawa
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Taste of Kerala and had a really good experience overall. The place serves tasty, authentic food with nice service. Due to the crowd, the staff does struggle a bit with serving everyone on time, but they still manage with a positive attitude.
We tried the Sunday Special Veg Banana Meal, Coconut Chilly Roasted Chicken with Kerala Paratha, and Chicken Kizhi Parotha. Every dish was absolutely delicious — rich flavours and true Kerala taste. We’ll definitely be visiting again!
A special mention to the manager, who was extremely warm and attentive. He personally checked on every table, and when he noticed we enjoyed the payasam, he even served us some extra. Such gestures really make the experience memorable. 💛🌴✨

featured_reviews.name: Hozefa Topiwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Taste of Kerala is truly a hidden gem! The place has a simple, no-frills setup — the ground floor is non-AC while the mezzanine floor is AC, though the ceiling upstairs is a bit low and seating is quite basic. But once the food arrives, you forget everything else!

The service here is absolutely fantastic. We were served by Raki, who was super enthusiastic and guided us through the menu with genuine passion. The restaurant is really lucky to have such a dedicated person on their team.

We ordered Chicken Pachamolak, Chicken Kerala, and Prawn Ghee Roast with wheat Laccha Kerala Paratha, and every dish was lip-smacking delicious. The authentic Kerala flavors were spot on!

They also serve complimentary Kerala papad, dahi boondi salad, and a variety of authentic chutneys, which are a must-try and perfectly complement the meal.

Overall, an amazing experience — fantastic food, warm service, and great value for money. We’ll definitely be visiting again and again!

featured_reviews.name: ittyadee bal
featured_reviews.review_text:
The menu shows a Veg Thali for ₹350, but on Sunday we were charged ₹440 for a “Sunday Special Thali.” The server did not inform us beforehand that the ₹350 thali was not available on Sundays. Only after we finished eating did he mention this.

It would have been better if this was clearly communicated before ordering. Also, the thali didn’t feel particularly “special” to justify the higher price. Transparency with customers would improve the experience.

featured_reviews.name: sankeertha varanasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai Masala is a new cozy Vegetarian restaurant in Narayanguda.
When you enter the place you witness fancy lightning column, sleek orange interiors which creates the fun, joy and playfulness atmosphere. Orange is a great colour choice because it stimulates the appetite and also encourages social interaction. Being foodaholic, I like everything from street food, fast food joints to cafe's and regular restaurants. This place is serving varity of cuisines with finest quality taste which makes this place interesting. If you wanna have thalis, proper north Indian and south indian food or any quick bites head here if you find yourself around. Each section on the menu has the timings written for when the dishes are available. Starting off with mocktails tried blue lagoon and Virgin mojito which were okay. Also, tried sweet Lassi and Oreo Milkshake according to me milkshake needs little improvisation.
Moving on to the appetizers section tried Crunchy manchurian dry which was spicy, crisp faultlessly tossed tasted great. Crispy Corn makes a ideal starter for veg's and it was palatable.
Chinese Bhel: This is my all time favourite chat which is made with fried noodles perked up with crunchy vegetables which was so appetizing.
Italian Paniyaram: This balls were made with green's and others veggies coated with breadcrumbs and deep fried topped with cheese.
Rumali Masala Papad topped with Indian chopped masala, lime, coriander and finely chopped fresh veggies. Nachos were served with cheese and bean's were flawless.
Vol-au-vents: It's a puff pastry stuffed with corn delivered maximum flavour when paired with cheese.
Vada Pav Dabeli Combo name itself says it's a combination snack the pav has both dabeli and vada pav flavour
Mumbai Masala Pizza: The pizza was quite good with a desi twist and loaded with lots of veggies, paneer and cheese.
Masala Garlic bread: Desi garlic bread tasted good and was having the perfect amount of the cheese and veggies added to it.
Pav Bhaji: It was served piping hot with flavourful bhaji
Moving to the much anticipated main course Mumbai Masala didn't disappoint one little bit. Veg Chatpat and Paneer Toofani were the curries of the day which were very well enjoyed with the hot, fluffy and soft breads. Paneer Toofani was having to kinds of curries half of the curry tasted like butter paneer masala and the other half tasted like palak paneer which was served in cabbage leaf. Coming to breads tried Lachha paratha, Kashmiri paratha, Lal mirch ka Paratha, kothmir butter naan, Chilli garlic naan, Masala kulcha, Kothmir butter roti and butter naan. Tried combination fried rice which was served with wet manchurian with an awesome presentation. Lastly, from the main course tried veg dum biryani which was soulful.
As, for desserts they don't have elaborate menu. Tried moong dal ka halwa set to perfection with drizzle of dry fruits. Sundae icecream was also good.
The service staff was pleasingly hospitable making sure there was never ever a moment where the diner's are waiting with empty plates.
Overall Taste:4/5
Service:5/5
Presentation:5/5

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.name: Manikandan
featured_reviews.review_text: Santosham - Satvik South Indian Restaurant near Marine Drive is a clean and comforting spot for authentic South Indian vegetarian food in South Mumbai. The restaurant keeps a simple, traditional feel without trying to be overly fancy, and the food is the main highlight. Located in Marine Lines, it’s convenient after a walk along Marine Drive or nearby sightseeing. Service is quick, portions are satisfying, and the overall experience feels homely and consistent without being overpriced. featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

The filter coffees (both cold and hot) were also delicious with the perfect froth on top! We also enjoyed the rose milk with chia seeds. 10/10 would recommend this place!

featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5

If you’re in Fort and craving authentic South Indian food, JM Idli Cafe is an absolute must-visit! It’s one of those rare places that combine delicious food, warm service, and genuine consistency — a true gem in the heart of Mumbai.

I’ve visited JM Idli Cafe multiple times, and every experience has been wonderful. Their menu offers a perfect blend of traditional South Indian favourites and creative variations. But the dish that truly wins my heart every single time is their Mysore Sada Cheese Dosa. It’s absolutely fantastic! The dosa is crisp, golden, and perfectly balanced — the slight spice of the Mysore chutney mixed with the smooth, melted cheese creates a unique and addictive flavour. You can immediately tell it’s made with care and fresh ingredients.

Their idlis are soft and fluffy, the sambar has that comforting homemade taste, and their chutneys are fresh, vibrant, and perfectly seasoned. Even simple dishes like the ghee dosa, upma, and pongal are prepared with attention to detail and taste just right.

The staff here deserve full appreciation as well — they’re polite, attentive, and always serve with a smile. You never have to wait too long, and they make sure every customer feels valued.

The café itself is clean, cosy, and welcoming — perfect for breakfast, lunch, or even a light evening meal. The prices are very reasonable for the quality and portion sizes, which makes it even more worth it.

Overall, JM Idli Cafe is the kind of place that keeps you coming back. Every visit feels satisfying and cheerful. If you love South Indian food or simply enjoy delicious, freshly made meals, you’ll love this spot. And if you visit, don’t miss their Mysore Sada Cheese Dosa — it’s honestly one of the best in Mumbai!

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is truly something special — an absolute must-visit.

Honestly, words fall short when I try to describe the experience we had here. The Sunday brunch completely won my heart. Every dish we tasted felt comforting, soulful, and almost like it was made at home with love. We just couldn’t stop — one dish after another, happily indulging and enjoying every bite.

What made it even more memorable was meeting the founders, Panchali and Vijay. They are incredibly warm, gracious, and genuinely passionate about what they’ve created. You can feel that warmth in the entire experience.

The menu, thoughtfully curated by Panchali herself, reflects that same authenticity — each dish carries a beautiful, home-cooked essence that’s rare to find.

featured_reviews.name: Darshana Rampuria
featured_reviews.review_text:
Oor is one of those places that quietly grows on you. Spread across two floors, it has these soft, calming vibes that almost transport you straight to Karnataka — minimal, warm, and unpretentious.

What really stayed with me though were the flavours. The rasam, uttapam, and filter coffee are absolute standouts — comforting, authentic, and the kind of dishes I’d happily go back for (and you definitely should try too).

It’s not just a meal here, it’s a slow, soulful experience.

featured_reviews.name: Sanjukta Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having lived in Karnataka for a decade has always left me craving for authentic food from there (and not the overhyped ones with long queues outside making regular food overpriced and exclusive). Oor lives up to its name - absolutely home like food that’s cleverly elevated and ambience with little details of the space reminding of kannadiga elements. I went for my birthday lunch and got delicious rasam rice with a side of banana poriyal. Absolutely delicious walnut halwa (a must have) and refreshing chaas. Every flavor will be familiar, homely and at the same time elevated. Staff is attentive and also mindful in that I felt at ease (and at home/oor). It was lovely to interact with the owner Panchaali and learn about her Mangalore roots and here’s hoping we will see some Mangalore OGs (like bun) on the menu :)

Cannot wait to be back again!

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited OOR Restaurant located at Kitab Mahal, Fort (near Azad Maidan), and it turned out to be a really satisfying South Indian food experience.

Cuisine:
OOR is known for authentic South Indian cuisine, focusing on traditional flavors, classic preparations, and comforting dishes that remind you of home-style food but with restaurant-quality execution.

Ambience:
The ambience is simple, clean, and welcoming. It has a calm and relaxed vibe, making it a great place for a casual meal with family, friends, or even a quick food stop while you’re around the Fort area. The space feels traditional yet comfortable, and perfect if you want to enjoy your food peacefully without too much noise.

What we tried:

☕ Filter Coffee – Strong, aromatic, and perfectly brewed. A must-have to complete the South Indian experience.

🧡 Steamed Idli – Soft, fluffy, and served fresh. Went really well with the chutneys and sambar.

🧅 Irulli Uttapam – Loaded with onions, nicely cooked, and full of flavor. Great texture and taste.

🥘 Paniyaram – Crispy outside, soft inside. A lovely traditional dish that was well made.

🌶️ Playa Uttapam – Unique and flavorful, nicely spiced and well presented.

🍛 OOR Thali – A complete meal with a variety of South Indian items. Perfect if you want to try multiple flavors at once. Very filling and satisfying.

Service & Management:
Service was smooth, staff was polite, and the overall management was well-handled. Food came on time and everything was served properly.

Overall:
If you’re someone who loves authentic South Indian food, OOR is definitely a spot to add to your bucket list — especially when you’re in the Fort area. Great food, good service, and a comforting dining experience. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

featured_reviews.name: Yash Popat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited OOR (Oor) in Fort for a South Indian dinner with my family, and it was outstanding. The ambiance is warm, minimal and earthy, setting the right mood for the meal.

The food was the highlight. Every dish tasted authentic, with clean flavours and perfect seasoning. The dosas were crisp, the chutneys fresh, and the mains had real depth and traditional taste.

Service was attentive and polite, and the portions were generous. If you want genuine South Indian flavours in a premium yet comforting setting, OOR at Fort is a great choice. Already looking forward to going back.

featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

Genuinely a top 5 all time restaurant for me. The food, the service, the ambience absolutely top tier. I have never had Indian food (from any region) as flavourful. The staff explained the concept and dishes incredibly well and the taster platter to help decide what to order was so fantastic. I would recommend this to absolutely everyone who lives in or is visiting Mumbai.

Thanks for an unforgettable night.

name: Bastian Ammakai

Rooted in the bold coastal flavours of Mangalore and the Konkan coast, we go beyond the usual idli-dosa spread to bring you honest home-style cooking, regional recipes, and dishes made with spices that actually tell a story. Whether you're dropping in for a relaxed breakfast or sitting down for a proper meal, the vibe is easygoing and the food is anything but ordinary. Our cocktails carry the same spirit - kokum, tamarind, and chilli shaken into something you haven't quite tasted before."

Aam & Ammakai is a limited seasonal spread built entirely around India's most beloved fruit, running through the kitchen, into the salad and desserts. The kind of menu that only exists for a few weeks every year, made with the kind of care and intuition that only Amma can bring.

Seasonal. Soulful. Straight from the heart. And gone before you know it.

Join us in Bandra West and taste the season before it slips away.

Amma went into the pantry. And came out with a crazy cocktail menu.

Tamarind. Curry leaf. Kokum. Coconut. Rasam. The staples that built South Indian kitchens for generations now shaken, stirred and reimagined into a bar menu that is as playful as it is surprising. Familiar on the nose. Completely unexpected in the glass.

The kind of cocktails you order once out of curiosity and reorder out of conviction.

Come curious. The bar menu at Ammakai will do the rest.

You cannot taste through a screen. But you can get a little closer to it.

Browse the Ammakai menu — modern South Indian dishes built on coastal spices and reimagined with a fresh perspective. The kind of food that sounds tempting on the page and tastes even better at the table. Consider this your first glimpse of what is waiting for you.

Take a look, choose your favourites, and join us in Bandra West for the full experience.

Most restaurants serve food. Ammakai feels like it has been waiting for you all day.

At Ammakai, rich South Indian flavours meet creative flair. Authentic coastal spices are given a fresh perspective, while every dish is crafted to delight beyond taste alone.

This is what happens when a cuisine rooted in warmth and tradition is handled with imagination and real care.

Your table is ready. We will see you in Bandra West.

You booked a table. You had plans after.

Ammakai — the kind of restaurant that makes leaving feel like a decision you keep putting off.

Come experience modern South Indian dining in Bandra West.

Filter coffee has always held a special place at Ammakai.

So naturally, we turned that love into a soft serve. Every bit of that deep, roasted, chicory kissed filter coffee flavour transformed into something soft, creamy, and unforgettable. The kind of dessert that feels deeply familiar yet pleasantly unexpected.

featured_reviews.name: Shaifa Hirji
featured_reviews.review_text:
The decor and overall aesthetic of this place are truly beautiful. The ambiance, design, and attention to detail make it feel like a high-end spot, and walking in, you definitely expect a premium dining experience. Unfortunately, while the space looks stunning, the actual experience did not live up to the expectations, especially considering the reputation and standard one would associate with a place like this.

The biggest issue by far was the number of bugs. There were so many insects flying around our table while we were eating, which completely ruined the experience. What made it even more uncomfortable was that the staff were actively killing bugs right next to us as we were dining, which felt extremely unhygienic and honestly quite disgusting. It completely took away from the enjoyment of the meal and made it hard to relax or even finish our food comfortably. For a restaurant of this level, this is simply unacceptable and needs serious attention.

In terms of the food, it was a mixed experience. The watermelon and pineapple juices were good — fresh, refreshing, and nicely prepared. The watermelon salad, however, lacked flavor and felt quite underwhelming, especially given how promising it sounded on the menu.

We ordered the edamame peas and the spicy chicken, and those dishes were actually quite good. They were well-cooked, flavorful, and enjoyable, which showed that the kitchen does have potential. However, good dishes alone cannot make up for poor hygiene standards and an uncomfortable dining environment.

The service also felt below expectation. It didn’t reflect the quality, attentiveness, or polish you would normally associate with a Bastian-level standard. Overall, the experience felt disorganized and lacking in the fine-dining attention to detail that one would expect.

In summary, while the decor is stunning and some of the food items were good, the bug issue and service quality seriously impacted the experience. It did not feel like a Bastian-standard restaurant, and until these issues are resolved, it’s hard to recommend. With better hygiene control, improved service, and more consistency in food quality, this place could truly live up to its potential — but for now, it unfortunately falls short.

Authentic Bengaluru-style Benne Dosa in Bandra West! This tiny, hidden gem near A Link Road serves incredibly crispy, ghee-roasted dosas that melt in your mouth. Their unique, punchy chutney replaces sambar, and the Almond Halwa is a must-try dessert. Fully Jain-friendly, it’s affordable, though expect a 30-45 min wait on weekends. Highly recommended for authentic, buttery South Indian comfort food!

Why you should visit:

The Food: Unbeatable crispy ghee dosa and delicious, unique chutney.
Best Dessert: The Almond Halwa is exceptional.

Convenience: Great Jain options.

Vibe: Very cozy and authentic (small seating capacity, so be ready to wait).

Price: Very reasonable for the quality.

Definitely, a 5-star experience!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Benne - Heritage Bangalore Dosa Overall Experience was great.This is one of the best South Indian restaurants I have tried especially for dosa and idli lovers.

1. Podi Masala Dosa:
Very crispy and full of flavour. This was the best dosa I have ever tried. Highly recommended.

2. Idli:
Very soft, fresh, and light. Tasted very good with chutney and sambar.

3. Ghee Podi Thatte Idli:
Extremely delicious and rich in taste. One of the best Thatte Idlis I have ever eaten. Must try.

4. Akki Roti:
Taste was okay, nothing special. Not recommended compared to other items.

5. Donne Pulav:
Pulav was okay, but the raita was very tasty and made the dish better.

👉Tips:
The restaurant closes at 3:30 PM and reopens at 5:30 PM. They also provide umbrellas during strong sunlight, which is helpful.

👉Suggestion:
It would be better if cold drinking water was provided.

featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best dosa places in Mumbai. We tried four dishes, and the garlic roast dosa was the best. The idli was extremely soft and tasted great with the coconut chutney.

The dosa was slightly thicker compared to other places, which worked well. One side was roasted while the other remained soft. Adding the chutneys made the overall experience even better.

featured_reviews.name: Jay Velwan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Benne Dosa Place and really enjoyed the food. I tried the Ghee Podi Masala Dosa and Garlic Podi Masala Dosa, and both were very flavorful and delicious. I also had the Ghee Podi Thatte Idli, which was the highlight of my visit — it was soft, tasty, and absolutely amazing.
Their red chutney was the real star of the meal. It paired perfectly with both the dosa and idli and tasted incredible.
I also tried the filter coffee, which was just average compared to how good the food was.
One downside is that the place is quite small. It gets crowded, and it can be difficult to stand and collect orders comfortably. The AC also didn’t seem to be working, which made it a bit uncomfortable.

Overall, the food quality is excellent, especially the Thatte Idli and red chutney, and I would definitely recommend trying them.

featured_reviews.name: Prabhjit Singh Modi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dosa and Thatte Idli both of them were good. What they could really add to the menu is some basic empathy.

I came from Vadodara after a 6-hour train journey and reached around 5:45 am. This was the first place I walked into straight from the railway station. At 6:00 am I politely asked the manager, the one with specs, if I could just sit in the corner since the space was empty and their setup was done. He flatly refused and said I could only enter at 7:00 am.

My back was hurting after the journey and I just needed a place to sit for a bit. It wouldn’t have cost them anything to show a little understanding. Instead, it was a straight no, no conversation.

If this were a smaller outlet, I’m pretty sure someone would’ve just said, “Haan bhai, sit.” Instead, he just didn’t allow it. No explanation, no actual rule, just a straight no. The place was empty, I wasn’t asking for free food, just a corner for 60 minutes after a 6-hour train ride. It honestly felt unnecessary and ego-driven.

That’s what happens when brands get big. A little success and suddenly basic decency becomes optional and Money gets to their head.

Massive respect though to the slim guy who seemed like the asst manager. He kept asking if I wanted to sit on his bike outside. That genuinely melted my heart. At least someone there understood basic humanity.

Food is good. The attitude needs serious work.

Not kidding, but Benne Mumbai has become our all-time spot for amazing benne dosas. After visiting around five times, I can confidently say they are very consistent with their quality and taste. The food is always fresh and satisfying, which keeps us coming back.

My recommendations:
• Benne Ghee Podi Masala Dosa
• Garlic Dosa
• Thatte Idli
• Medu Vada (perfectly crispy)
• Filter Kaapi Ice Cream

Even their chutneys are really good and pair perfectly with the dishes.
